photons.note: cf = cloud-free scene at the same campaign and seeds; iid = per-pass independent clouds scored with the OU covariance (sigma_cl held at the OU fiducial value), so only the temporal structure of the weather changes

wallclock.note: cf = cloud-free scene at the same campaign and seeds; iid = per-pass independent clouds scored with the OU covariance (sigma_cl held at the OU fiducial value), so only the temporal structure of the weather changes

audit.json.cadence_note: arm A holds mp*ts = 8 h per raster position and lets the wall clock exceed 90 d; arm B holds wall <= 90 d and lets ts fall. They cannot both hold.

latband.note: band r is computed on the SAME archived reconstructions as the headline numbers, restricted to the band; weight is the campaign-mean column energy of F, so zero weight means the raster never samples the band; gain is sd(recon)/sd(truth) within the band, which Pearson r cannot see

ledger.note: N_eff = mp^2/(mp + 2 sum_k (mp-k) exp(-k dt/tau)) with dt the FULL pass time between revisits of one raster position; the mp revisits of a pixel are 5.47 d apart at the fiducial campaign, i.e. only ~1.4 cloud-correlation times, so they are NOT independent looks and the gain from mp saturates.

nulls.note: with 10 paired seeds the exact minimum two-sided sign-flip p is 1.95e-3; the cloud-only null has n=40 realizations so its smallest attainable rank p is 1/41

resolution.band_weighting_note: weighted = sum (2l+1) r(l) / sum (2l+1) over the band; unweighted = arithmetic mean of the degrees in the band. The two differ most at high l, which is why an unweighted mean of 13-16 and 17-20 can conceal a resolved gain in 13-16.
resolution.l_eff_cf_note: null means NO crossing: on a 36x72 grid the cloud-free r(l) never falls below 0.90 within the supported band, so an effective degree is undefined and is reported as null rather than as a fabricated number. The ceiling is the minimum of the curve, r_cf_min, at l_at_r_cf_min.

robust_debias.note: Pearson r is invariant to the affine debiasing error; bias/RMSE/contrast are what move

sigma_sensitivity.note: sigma_cl is the ASSUMED cloud amplitude; r is scored against truth while chi2 is the whitened objective under that same assumed covariance

static_reference.note: stat = frozen planet, no weather, identical dose per raster position; rot = same estimator on the rotating cloud-free campaign; cloud = fiducial rotating cloudy campaign

systematics.note: amplitudes are fractional residuals OF THE CORONAL BACKGROUND; multiply by Qcor/Qexo = 7.7403e4 to get planet-reference units

weather.note: true weather field varied in spatial correlation length, advection rate and decorrelation time; each variant scored with the fiducial OU climatology (misspecified) and with its own (recalibrated)

deflation_diag.json.note: rank/93.75% framing replaced by (i) rank, which profiling does not change, and (ii) the constant-mode gain ratio, which is what profiling actually removes

profiling.nullity_note: the un-profiled null space is a property of the grid and the circular raster, not of the nuisance profiling; profiling adds no null directions

caveats: Markov model uses simplified 3-state transition matrix; real cloud physics is more complex
Hawkes excitation parameter (0.3) is assumed; not calibrated to Earth data
Topographic anchor uses albedo as proxy for orography; real mountains have different signatures

sigma_cl is the OU-calibrated value and is NOT recalibrated per model, so the realized final-frame cover differs by arm (OU 0.5577, Markov 0.3692, Hawkes 0.6169, topo 0.5353, strong anchor 0.5201); absolute r across arms is therefore a sensitivity range, not a controlled A/B test
Each model runs simulate_dataset independently; cloud fields are not shared across models

The anchored arm is OU noise plus a STATIC orographic offset; it has no rotational phase locking, so it neither reproduces nor refutes the spine's surf_coupling collapse case (read from audit.robust_clim instead)
10 noise seeds; the collapse reference is the spine's 10-seed ensemble, so the two are not paired

note: static orographic offset doubled; NOT a phase-locking test

caveats: Baumbert-Allen density model is for quiet Sun; active regions can have 10x higher density.
Coronal turbulence and density fluctuations are not modeled; only the mean deflection is computed.
Phase screen is computed at b=1.5 R_sun; the full ring samples a range of b.

The weak-refraction approximation (alpha < 1 rad) fails at lambda > 1.594 m (188 MHz) at b=1.5 R_sun; everything on the radio side of that limit in this sweep is an extrapolation of the lambda^2 scaling, not a valid prediction.
At radio frequencies (lambda > model_valid_below_m), full ray-tracing is needed.
The Strehl and photometric-error columns are single-screen estimates at one impact parameter; they bound the chromatic term but do not enter the inversion.

eps_equiv_coronal at 1 um is 8.602e-14 coronal units, which is 1.16e+05x BELOW the smallest injected residual on the archived systematics grid (1.0e-08 coronal units). The archived drift curve is therefore not sampled anywhere near the refractive level: delta_r_from_base is a clamp to the base point, not a measured loss, and the correct statement is that refraction is outside the range this pipeline has ever tested.
Limb-darkening coefficients are approximate (Claret 2000 tables at 1 um); wavelength-dependent coefficients would change the result.

Solar J2 oblateness is NOT applied to the shipped kernel: the operator stays axisymmetric. solar_oblateness_factor() is used only to bound the omitted term at the adopted dynamical J2 = 2.2e-07, whose largest effect on the Einstein-ring radius is 5.889e-04 m = 2.816e-05 cells at n=64, i.e. below one imaging cell.
Occultation of the limb ring by a planet or the Moon is not modelled in this module at all; it requires a specific ephemeris and observer timeline and is left to the ephemeris module.
The disk-integrated kernel is a simplified model; a full wave-optics treatment would be needed for precise predictions.
The offdiag_rel_err is computed vs the point kernel; comparison with the cell-mean kernel would give a different value.
No ephemeris package used; geometry computed from analytic elements + J2000 obliquity 23.43928 deg.
Access window model is simplified; actual windows depend on spacecraft trajectory and Sun avoidance constraints.
Plane-change delta-v uses impulsive approximation; finite-burn trajectories would cost more.
z drift assumes constant velocity; actual trajectory includes gravitational acceleration from the Sun.
The spin-ephemeris phase requirement is derived from the timing error, not from a full navigation analysis.

feasibility_score here is SNR x access_window_fraction / (1 + impulsive plane-change dv in km/s), with plane-change dv from the image-plane transverse velocity, NOT the 1.34-5.81 km/s 90-day transfer budget the manuscript's mission-rule score uses. The two proxies order the table differently (Ross 128 b first here, GJ 273 b first there) because they price different quantities; neither is a trajectory optimisation and no single ranking should be quoted as the target list.
Evidence uses deflated system (matching the deflate solver convention)
Constant offset in log-evidence is dropped (only relative comparison matters)
Archived lamsweep parts reused for r/SSIM/χ² comparison columns
Grid spans 1e-05..3e-01; the evidence maximum and the r/SSIM maxima lie ON that boundary, so they are edge locations, not located optima (chi2 is the only interior one)
10 noise seeds

headline.conclusion: Log-evidence DECREASES monotonically across the grid (1e-05 to 3e-01) in the cloudy case, so its maximum is the left edge lambda=1e-05, not an interior optimum; cloud-free it is decreasing with maximum lambda=1e-05. chi2 alone has an interior minimum (lambda=1e-01); r and SSIM both rise to the right edge (lambda=3e-01). The determinant term therefore does not locate a preferred smoothing scale on this grid: an evidence-based rule would drive the solver to the weakest regularisation allowed, which is the opposite of what the original wording claimed. No truth-blind criterion is established here; the grid has to be extended in both directions before any of these locations can be called an optimum.

provenance.prior_convention: Tikhonov/ridge with Laplacian precision λLᵀL, λ_eff = λ tr(A)/tr(LtL)

caveats: CRLB cadence sweep uses analytic N_eff scaling calibrated at the fiducial per-pixel variance, not full Fisher builds at each point, so it inherits the scaling problem stated next.

The per-pixel CRLB from pinv(J) is NOT a comparable floor for this estimator: mean(diag V) = 4.6185e+01 exceeds var(truth) = 3.6627e-02 by 1260.9x, so the bound is weaker than predicting the constant map and r_pred is identically zero. J has nullity 288 and an infinite condition number, and pinv gives those 144 directions zero variance while the near-degenerate ones reach 7.57e+03 (median of the non-zero diagonal 1.26e-01). The archived regularised fit actually achieves (1-r^2)var = 3.225e-02 at M_p=16, i.e. 7.0e-04 of that pseudo-inverse bound; a biased estimator 'beating' an unbiased bound by three decades is the signature of the wrong yardstick, not of super-efficiency.

What this module does establish is the information accounting: trace(J_prof)/trace(J_unprof) and its agreement with the independent normal-matrix audit. The variance floor it also computes is reported for completeness and marked degenerate.
nrmse_sim derived from archived r_sim as sqrt(1 - r^2); archived cadence files do not store nrmse directly.
Aliasing explanation of M_p=8 non-monotonicity is qualitative; a full harmonic analysis would be needed for rigorous proof.
Fisher matrix built with constant sigma_k (not signal-dependent noise); valid in the background-dominated regime Q_cor >> Q_exo.
frobenius_ratio = trace(J_prof)/trace(J_unprof) = 0.662 is distinct from profiling constant-mode survival (free=0.0206, anchored=0.8472).
ROC AUC and area/contrast metrics require the truth map; they are not estimable in flight
d' uses the same land/ocean threshold (truth_c > 0.15) as S.detection_dprime
Label-permutation null uses 2000 permutations per seed (floor 1/2001 = 5.0e-4)
Physical null ensemble has 40 realisations (p-value floor 1/41 = 0.0244)
Histogram moments computed on mid-latitude (|lat| <= 60 deg) pixels only

Area recovery and its false-positive rate classify the retrieved map at its own MEDIAN, an uncalibrated balanced split: they say how the retrieved ordering of pixels partitions the true classes, not whether a thresholded map would be usable. Contrast recovery uses the truth labels for both groups and is the load-bearing number of the two.

Maps are read from results/parts/clouds_f*_s*.npz, where run_experiments stores them AFTER debiasing; _surface_map verifies that against the archived bias instead of re-applying the transform, which would leave r, d' and AUC untouched and corrupt only the albedo-scale statistics.
Paired at ONE seed (the tier's first); the ensemble value is quoted separately and is context, not the comparison.
NOT a test of the surface-coupling (phase-locking) collapse: the fiducial CloudModel has surf_coupling=0, so its screens are not rotationally locked and -0.198 cannot be reproduced or refuted here.
The Airy FWHM is set equal to the SGL image-plane pitch DIMG/n by construction; this is a matched-resolution swap, not a realistic conventional-telescope design study.
The Airy kernel is a far-field diffraction pattern; near-field SGL effects, solar J2/limb structure and occultation are neglected.
The forward operator is rebuilt from scratch, so operator-construction differences beyond the kernel itself may contribute to the loss.
Only the profiled solver is tested; white-noise and deflation baselines are not re-run under the alternative kernel.
TV uses post-processing of TDI solution (not joint optimization)
Sparse coding learns dictionary from TDI solution (circular)
Learned denoiser: not_established (requires training set)
4 noise seeds

headline.conclusion: Ranked by r: sparse r=0.3512, TDI r=0.3491, TV r=0.3309. TDI-TV paired +0.0183 [+0.0160, +0.0213] sign-test p=0.125 on 4 seeds; TDI-sparse paired -0.0020 [-0.0083, +0.0047] sign-test p=1.000. This is NOT a clean prior bake-off: the TV arm post-processes the TDI map, and the sparse dictionary is learned from it, so a margin either way partly measures the operator rather than an independent prior. At four noise seeds no pairing here can be significant (exact sign-test floor p=0.125), and the sparse arm is not distinguishable from TDI.

learned.reason: not_established: requires training set of truth/reconstruction pairs

caveats: Full simulation with custom F not performed (too expensive)
N_eff comparison is the primary metric; no paired Delta r is reported
Phase aliasing analysis is exact for uniform spacing
6 noise seeds

headline.conclusion: N_eff improvement from optimized scheduling is <1% (5.097 -> 5.139) at M_p=8. The M_p=8 non-monotonicity of the cadence law is NOT a scheduling artifact but a phase-grid aliasing effect: at M_p=8 the harmonic m=8 falls exactly on the sampling grid (45 deg phase spacing), so no reordering of the dwells within that M_p can un-alias it; this module does not re-simulate the map, so the reconstruction contrast it reports is N_eff plus the harmonic argument, not a paired Delta r

caveats: Mode-SNR gain computed in harmonic domain; assumes independent noise per spacecraft
Joint inversion attempted on 2 seeds for N=2 only (memory constraint); quote joint_delta_r_paired, not joint_delta_r_ensemble, for any same-photons claim
Ring-radius offsets span 0.3 to 2.0 times fiducial pitch (0.3-2.0 × 20.9 m = 6-42 m)
Physically, offsets should span the Einstein ring radius (~1.3 km at z=650 AU)
Station-keeping tolerance computed from kernel sensitivity dK/K = -drho/rho
Formation-control sweep uses random perturbation with fixed seed 42
Distance uncertainty: assumed 5% fractional (Gaussian) -- targets.json does not carry per-target distance errors
M sin i uncertainty: assumed 10% fractional (Gaussian) -- actual errors depend on RV precision and are target-specific
Chen & Kipping Terran branch dispersion 4.03% applied to targets below transition
Chen & Kipping Neptunian branch dispersion 14.60% applied to targets above transition (rocky EXTRAPOLATION)
Albedo prior: uniform over [0.15, 0.45], matching the paper's bounded range
No per-target catalogue covariance matrices available -- each parameter drawn independently
De-inclination factor used as fixed constant (1.0978), not propagated (its uncertainty is negligible)
Reachability score is a simple 1/(1+dv) heuristic, not a full trajectory optimization

not_established.catalogue_covariance_matrices: Not available in the repository; parameters treated as independent
not_established.per_target_distance_errors: targets.json does not carry per-target distance uncertainties; assumed 5% Gaussian
not_established.per_target_msini_errors: targets.json does not carry per-target M sin i uncertainties; assumed 10% Gaussian
not_established.spectral_energy_distribution: Wavelength-dependent photon correction not implemented (requires Turyshev & Toth 2022c/2023b)

caveats: The r_loss_* fields linearise the phase-error response at the archived local slope measured from robprof_s0.npz (0.00192 per degree, two-sided over +/-5 deg); the response is visibly non-linear and asymmetric beyond a few degrees, so these numbers are only meaningful for the sub-degree phase errors a real timing budget produces.

Downlink volume is stated in two declared record conventions: 32 B/sample (time tag, value, uncertainty, bookkeeping; this is what raw_volume_mb reports) and 4 B/sample (float32 value only, value_only_volume_mb). Neither assumes lossless compression.

The gridded product holds one float32 per pixel per pass, which is exactly as many numbers as the campaign has measurements (n^2*mp = nbin*mp*nsc), so the value-only chain compresses by 1.00x and bookkept_over_binned measures the bookkeeping overhead, not a compression gain.
Kinematic check uses idealised rest-to-rest maneuver; actual trajectory includes gravity and drag.
The timing budget does not include thermal settling or detector readout time.
The 8.64 s worst-case timing error is derived as 1e-4 * Prot; the actual requirement depends on the science goal.
Dominant cloudy uncertainty is within-map (noise seeds): between-map sd 0.02118 vs within-map (noise-seed) sd 0.02549; cloud-free between-map (0.00374 vs 0.00054)

Profiled-minus-deflate sign is NOT stable across truth maps (3 positive, 2 negative of 5 maps): mean difference +3.72e-06, member-to-member scatter 2.80e-04; the two solvers are indistinguishable under a geography change, which is a weaker statement than 'profiled is better'
Validation: truth_seed=7 reproduces archived fiducial to <1e-6
Full tier reduced to 5 truth x 4 noise seeds (20 members); the solve took 13.7 min, so the grid is a budget decision, not a convergence check

headline.conclusion: Across 5 independent planetary geographies the cloudy profiled correlation is 0.3173 +/- 0.0304 (sd), of which 0.0212 is between maps and 0.0255 within-map; the fiducial map ranks 1 of 5 on this metric. The profiled-minus-deflate gap is +3.72e-06 cloudy and +4.88e-05 cloud-free, with the sign stable across maps in the cloud-free case only, so the solver comparison is a null result under a geography change, while the fiducial map's place at the top of the ensemble is a real property of that map and not of the noise.

precision.json.nullity_note: unregularized nullity = 2 x the identically-zero polar columns; the partners are their near-degenerate twins

regime.note: reduced size; the fiducial n=64 design would need ~2.8 GB in two float64 copies

deinclination.note: mean of the RATIO, not ratio of the means; the mean diverges for alpha >= 1

meta.disclaimer: Nominal proxies only.  The scalar SNR rule is a bolometric scalar, not a wavelength-integrated photon forecast (that needs the spectral SGL treatment, Turyshev & Toth 2022c PRD 106 044059; Turyshev & Toth 2023b PRD 107 104063).  De-inclination factors are conditional geometric ratios at fixed minimum mass on a single branch, not a posterior; radii above the 2.04 M_earth Terran/Neptunian transition are rocky EXTRAPOLATIONS, not the published probabilistic model.  The albedo x radius brackets are bounded intervals over stated ranges and carry no confidence level.
